question:
A 58-year-old woman visits her physician with persistent bone pain, loss of appetite, and hiccups that
began 3 months ago and have progressively worsened. She also reports chest pain, generalized
itching, and dry skin. Her medical history includes frequent fractures, poorly controlled hypertension,
and unmanaged type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has not taken any medications or seen a doctor in 20
years. On physical examination, she has significant conjunctival pallor, prominent zygomatic bones,
grade 3 asterixis, and a gray-brown discoloration of her skin. A loud pericardial friction rub is heard at
the lower left sternal border. Laboratory findings are as follows: | | | | --- | --- | | Sodium | 146 mEq/L | |
Chloride | 104 mEq/L | | BUN | 122 mg/dL | | Calcium | 7.8 mg/dL | | Uric acid | 3.4 mg/dL | | Potassium |
5.8 mEq/L | | Bicarbonate | 16 mmol/L | | Creatinine | 5.8 mg/dL | | Magnesium | 1.1 mEq/L | |
Hemoglobin | 8.6 g/dL | A peripheral blood smear reveals normocytic normochromic anemia. A lumbar
spine radiograph demonstrates multiple well-defined cystic lesions and subperiosteal thinning. What is

the most likely underlying cause of these radiographic findings? Answer Choices: (A)
Hormone-mediated fibrous replacement of bone (B) Chronic metabolic acidosis leading to bone
demineralization (C) Defective collagen synthesis in bone matrix due to anemia (D) Impaired carbonic
anhydrase activity in osteoclasts (E) Excessive osteoclastic activity due to vitamin D deficiency (F)
Dysfunctional osteoblast activity secondary to hypermagnesemia (G) Secondary hyperparathyroidism
due to chronic kidney disease (H) Impaired calcium absorption due to chronic gastrointestinal disease
(I) Defective mineralization of osteoid secondary to hormone deficiency (J) Increased osteoid
deposition in response to acidosis
 A. Defective collagen synthesis in bone matrix due to anemia
B. Increased osteoid deposition in response to acidosis
C. Dysfunctional osteoblast activity secondary to hypermagnesemia
D. Hormone-mediated fibrous replacement of bone
E. Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic kidney disease
F. Chronic metabolic acidosis leading to bone demineralization
G. Defective mineralization of osteoid secondary to hormone deficiency
H. Excessive osteoclastic activity due to vitamin D deficiency
I. Impaired carbonic anhydrase activity in osteoclasts
J. Impaired calcium absorption due to chronic gastrointestinal disease
